You are reverse-engineering the behavior of a compiled binary at /workspace/executable (call it as ./executable from /workspace).
It is "gomplate", a Go text/template renderer. Documentation lives in /workspace/docs/content/.

HARD RULES (violating them fails the whole project):
- You MUST NOT use the network, MUST NOT search the web, MUST NOT download or read the original gomplate source from anywhere.
- You MUST NOT decompile, disassemble, objdump, strace, ltrace, nm, strings(1), or otherwise statically analyze ./executable.
- You may ONLY run ./executable with normal CLI arguments and observe stdout/stderr/exit code, and read the bundled docs.

How to invoke: ./executable -i '<template>'   (prints rendered result to stdout)
Errors are logged to stderr as JSON: {"time":...,"level":"ERROR","msg":"","err":"..."} and exit code 1.
Useful trick: wrap results with printf "%T / %#v" to learn the concrete Go type a function returns, e.g.
  ./executable -i '{{ printf "%T" (conv.ToInt "5") }}'
Another: {{ test.Kind x }} and {{ test.IsKind "int" x }} reveal reflect kinds.

YOUR OUTPUT: write a thorough markdown spec file. Be exhaustive and precise: this spec is the ONLY thing a
separate implementer agent will see — they will not have access to the binary at first. Every fact must be
concrete and verified by an actual command you ran.

For EVERY function in your assigned area document:
1. Exact name(s) including aliases (verify each alias actually exists in THIS build — docs are stale, some
   documented functions were removed; e.g. conv.Bool does NOT exist here).
2. Exact parameter order and count, including variadic behavior and gomplate's "data is the LAST argument"
   pipeline convention. Verify by experiment, not by reading docs.
3. The concrete Go return type (use printf "%T").
4. Type coercion rules for inputs (what happens with int vs string vs float vs bool vs nil vs slice vs map).
5. Error messages VERBATIM (copy the exact "err" string), and whether it errors vs returns zero value.
6. Edge cases: empty string, empty slice, nil, negative numbers, unicode/multibyte, very large numbers,
   wrong arg count, wrong types.
7. At least 5-15 concrete verified examples per function in the form:
   | template | output |
   Use a fenced table or list. Copy outputs EXACTLY (including whitespace/newlines; note trailing newlines).

Finish the spec with a "GOTCHAS" section listing anything surprising an implementer would get wrong.
Do not summarize or truncate — length is good. Aim for a very detailed document.

YOUR ASSIGNED AREA: regexp
Relevant docs: /workspace/docs/content/functions/regexp.md (read it first to get the function list, then verify each against the binary).
Focus on Find/FindAll/Match/QuoteMeta/Replace/ReplaceLiteral/Split. Verify arg order carefully (regex first? last?). Test capture group expansion $1 in Replace vs ReplaceLiteral, the n argument in FindAll/Split, and invalid-regex error text.

Write your spec to /tmp/spec/regexp.md using the Write tool. Then reply with just a one-paragraph summary of what you covered and anything you could not determine.

2	title: regexp functions
3	menu:
4	  main:
5	    parent: functions
6	---
7	
8	These functions allow user you to search and modify text with regular expressions.
9	
10	The syntax of the regular expressions accepted is [Go's `regexp` syntax](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/syntax/#hdr-Syntax),
11	and is the same general syntax used by Perl, Python, and other languages.
12	
13	## `regexp.Find`
14	
15	Returns a string holding the text of the leftmost match in `input`
16	of the regular expression `expression`.
17	
18	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
19	[`regexp.FindString`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/#Regexp.FindString) function.
20	
21	_Added in gomplate [v3.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.1.0)_
22	### Usage
23	
24	```
25	regexp.Find expression input
26	```
27	```
28	input | regexp.Find expression
29	```
30	
31	### Arguments
32	
33	| name | description |
34	|------|-------------|
35	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression |
36	| `input` | _(required)_ The input to search |
37	
38	### Examples
39	
40	```console
41	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.Find "[a-z]{3}" "foobar"}}'
42	foo
43	```
44	```console
45	$ gomplate -i 'no {{ "will not match" | regexp.Find "[0-9]" }}numbers'
46	no numbers
47	```
48	
49	## `regexp.FindAll`
50	
51	Returns a list of all successive matches of the regular expression.
52	
53	This can be called with 2 or 3 arguments. When called with 2 arguments, the
54	`n` argument (number of matches) will be set to `-1`, causing all matches
55	to be returned.
56	
57	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
58	[`regexp.FindAllString`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp#Regexp.FindAllString) function.
59	
60	_Added in gomplate [v3.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.1.0)_
61	### Usage
62	
63	```
64	regexp.FindAll expression [n] input
65	```
66	```
67	input | regexp.FindAll expression [n]
68	```
69	
70	### Arguments
71	
72	| name | description |
73	|------|-------------|
74	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression |
75	| `n` | _(optional)_ The number of matches to return |
76	| `input` | _(required)_ The input to search |
77	
78	### Examples
79	
80	```console
81	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.FindAll "[a-z]{3}" "foobar" | toJSON}}'
82	["foo", "bar"]
83	```
84	```console
85	$ gomplate -i '{{ "foo bar baz qux" | regexp.FindAll "[a-z]{3}" 3 | toJSON}}'
86	["foo", "bar", "baz"]
87	```
88	
89	## `regexp.Match`
90	
91	Returns `true` if a given regular expression matches a given input.
92	
93	This returns a boolean which can be used in an `if` condition, for example.
94	
95	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
96	### Usage
97	
98	```
99	regexp.Match expression input
100	```
101	```
102	input | regexp.Match expression
103	```
104	
105	### Arguments
106	
107	| name | description |
108	|------|-------------|
109	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression |
110	| `input` | _(required)_ The input to test |
111	
112	### Examples
113	
114	```console
115	$ gomplate -i '{{ $u := env.Env.USER }}{{if ($u | regexp.Match `^h`) }}username ({{ $u }}) starts with h!{{end}}'
116	username (hairyhenderson) starts with h!
117	```
118	
119	## `regexp.QuoteMeta`
120	
121	Escapes all regular expression metacharacters in the input. The returned string is a regular expression matching the literal text.
122	
123	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
124	[`regexp.QuoteMeta`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp#QuoteMeta) function.
125	
126	_Added in gomplate [v3.7.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.7.0)_
127	### Usage
128	
129	```
130	regexp.QuoteMeta input
131	```
132	```
133	input | regexp.QuoteMeta
134	```
135	
136	### Arguments
137	
138	| name | description |
139	|------|-------------|
140	| `input` | _(required)_ The input to escape |
141	
142	### Examples
143	
144	```console
145	$ gomplate -i '{{ `{hello}` | regexp.QuoteMeta }}'
146	\{hello\}
147	```
148	
149	## `regexp.Replace`
150	
151	Replaces matches of a regular expression with the replacement string.
152	
153	The replacement is substituted after expanding variables beginning with `$`.
154	
155	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
156	[`regexp.ReplaceAllString`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/#Regexp.ReplaceAllString) function.
157	
158	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
159	### Usage
160	
161	```
162	regexp.Replace expression replacement input
163	```
164	```
165	input | regexp.Replace expression replacement
166	```
167	
168	### Arguments
169	
170	| name | description |
171	|------|-------------|
172	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression string |
173	| `replacement` | _(required)_ The replacement string |
174	| `input` | _(required)_ The input string to operate on |
175	
176	### Examples
177	
178	```console
179	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.Replace "(foo)bar" "$1" "foobar"}}'
180	foo
181	```
182	```console
183	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.Replace "(?P<first>[a-zA-Z]+) (?P<last>[a-zA-Z]+)" "${last}, ${first}" "Alan Turing"}}'
184	Turing, Alan
185	```
186	
187	## `regexp.ReplaceLiteral`
188	
189	Replaces matches of a regular expression with the replacement string.
190	
191	The replacement is substituted directly, without expanding variables
192	beginning with `$`.
193	
194	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
195	[`regexp.ReplaceAllLiteralString`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/#Regexp.ReplaceAllLiteralString) function.
196	
197	_Added in gomplate [v3.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.1.0)_
198	### Usage
199	
200	```
201	regexp.ReplaceLiteral expression replacement input
202	```
203	```
204	input | regexp.ReplaceLiteral expression replacement
205	```
206	
207	### Arguments
208	
209	| name | description |
210	|------|-------------|
211	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression string |
212	| `replacement` | _(required)_ The replacement string |
213	| `input` | _(required)_ The input string to operate on |
214	
215	### Examples
216	
217	```console
218	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.ReplaceLiteral "(foo)bar" "$1" "foobar"}}'
219	$1
220	```
221	```console
222	$ gomplate -i '{{ `foo.bar,baz` | regexp.ReplaceLiteral `\W` `$` }}'
223	foo$bar$baz
224	```
225	
226	## `regexp.Split`
227	
228	Splits `input` into sub-strings, separated by the expression.
229	
230	This can be called with 2 or 3 arguments. When called with 2 arguments, the
231	`n` argument (number of matches) will be set to `-1`, causing all sub-strings
232	to be returned.
233	
234	This is equivalent to [`strings.SplitN`](../strings/#stringssplitn),
235	except that regular expressions are supported.
236	
237	This function provides the same behaviour as Go's
238	[`regexp.Split`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/#Regexp.Split) function.
239	
240	_Added in gomplate [v3.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.1.0)_
241	### Usage
242	
243	```
244	regexp.Split expression [n] input
245	```
246	```
247	input | regexp.Split expression [n]
248	```
249	
250	### Arguments
251	
252	| name | description |
253	|------|-------------|
254	| `expression` | _(required)_ The regular expression |
255	| `n` | _(optional)_ The number of matches to return |
256	| `input` | _(required)_ The input to search |
257	
258	### Examples
259	
260	```console
261	$ gomplate -i '{{ regexp.Split `[\s,.]` "foo bar,baz.qux" | toJSON}}'
262	["foo","bar","baz","qux"]
263	```
264	```console
265	$ gomplate -i '{{ "foo bar.baz,qux" | regexp.Split `[\s,.]` 3 | toJSON}}'
266	["foo","bar","baz"]
267	```
